key_insight: AISPA is a user-centric audit framework that systematically evaluates hidden system prompts in commercial LLM applications, revealing that protective instructions are common but often incomplete and frequently coexist with user-harming ones.
engineering_relevance: For AI product teams, the paper shows that prompt governance needs measurable auditing standards to improve transparency, user safety, and accountability in deployed systems.
method: Defined AISPA to audit system prompt instructions across 8 user-relevant dimensions
Labeled each instruction as protective or problematic
Applied the framework to 3,249 instructions from 88 commercial AI products
evidence_signal: The authors analyzed 3,249 system-prompt instructions across 88 commercial products and found that 98.9% of products had at least one protective instruction, but only 24% covered all eight AISPA dimensions.
watch_item: The audit relies on available system prompts and instruction-level classification, so results may vary with prompt access, versioning, and subjective labeling boundaries.
paper_title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
